BUG FOUND AND FIXED before stage 8 could produce correct output: 34 part labels (across 21 multi-part items, spanning ex_3.11, ex_3.20, q_3.1.1/1.4/1.5/1.6, q_3.2.1/2.2/2.3/2.7/2.14/2.19, q_3.3.1/3.2/3.3/3.5/3.6/3.7/3.8/3.10, q_3.9.7) had been silently dropped somewhere between 02_extract and 04_combined - traced to pipeline.mdio._node_to_item's Part-parsing, which only ever reads a part's `label` attribute (schema.Part has no `number` field), while several of stage 2's extraction batches had used `:::part{number="(i)"}` instead of `:::part{label="(i)"}` for their sub-part identifiers - a naming inconsistency between batches at the very first stage that this pipeline's own mechanical round-trip (stage 3 split -> stage 4 combine, both 'no model call, pure function' per CLAUDE.md) then silently discarded, since Pydantic's Part model has nowhere to put an unrecognized attribute. The math/text content of every affected part was completely correct and untouched throughout - only the '(i)'/'(ii)'/'(a)'/'(b)' identifier distinguishing which part is which was lost, surfacing only now because stage 8 is the first stage that actually surfaces a part's `label` field on its own (as JSON, for stage 9 to render) rather than passing the whole container through as opaque markdown. Fixed by rebuilding the correct number->label mapping directly from 02_extract/chapter.hi.md (which still has every part's original `number=` attribute, untouched since it predates the mdio round-trip that dropped it) and reapplying it, by item id and part position/order (order was never lost, only the label attribute), onto every bare `:::part` line in 07_format/structured.hi.md directly - a metadata/attribute restoration, not a content rewrite: no word, digit, symbol, math span or table was touched (protect.parity before/after the fix: zero drift), and tag._parse remained valid throughout. All 32 previously-bare parts (plus the 2 in q_3.9.7 fixed individually just before this batch fix was written) now carry their correct original label. FLAGGING for whoever next touches pipeline/mdio.py or step_2/extract.md: _node_to_item's Part construction should either accept `number` as a fallback alias for `label` (matching how a part's identifier is genuinely used interchangeably across this pipeline's own chapters - some batches write `label=`, some write `number=`, for what is semantically the same thing), or step_2/extract.md should state a single required attribute name so this cannot recur silently in a future chapter's extraction batches.

Second bug found and fixed in stage 8's own hand-rolled JSON walker (after the part-label restoration already recorded in the format_correction entry above): 71 answer flow segments (across both item-level and part-level answers) carried a raw, unconverted '**उत्तर:**' ('**Answer:**') markdown prefix - pipeline.render.render_item() bakes this literal prefix into every :::answer block's body text (documented in mdio.py's own _strip_answer_prefix() and its comment: unlike :::solution, which correctly carries its label as a separate attribute, :::answer's label is baked into the text itself and must be stripped by the reader). PRIMARY NEW WORK - genuine matrix rendering: this chapter's dominant content shape (854 of 863 \begin{array} occurrences are \left[...\right]-bracketed matrices) had NO prior-chapter precedent; maths-12-2's own generic \begin{env} handler just concatenates cells with no column separation at all (fine for its own aligned/gathered equation-display use, unreadable for an actual matrix - confirmed for real: ex_3.1's 3x2 data matrix rendered as the single glued token 'A = [3025 2531 2726]' before this fix, a materially wrong-looking result, not just ugly). Added a dedicated text-level pre-pass (_extract_matrices/_find_matrix_spans/_render_matrix in latex.py) that detects a genuine \left[\begin{array}{colspec}...\end{array}\right] span specifically (never a bare \begin{array} used for ordinary equation alignment, which still goes through the pre-existing generic handler unchanged), recursively converts each cell's own content, and renders it as a real CSS grid (.s97/.s98) with the column count taken from the colspec, flanked by two CSS-drawn square brackets (.s95/.s96, plain borders stretched to the grid's full height via flex align-items:stretch) wrapped in one inline-flex unit (.s94, white-space:nowrap + overflow-x:auto safety net + break-inside:avoid, matching the existing .s31/.s90 fraction/sqrt page-break and line-wrap protections). SECOND BUG FOUND AND FIXED (pre-existing in maths-12-2's own code, newly exposed by this chapter's content): the generic \begin{env} handler's row-splitting (`body.split('\\\\')`) does not respect a NESTED \begin{...}...\end{...} block's own internal row separators - caught for real on ex_3.11 part (iii) and ex_3.19 (both use a small bare \begin{array}{c|cc}...\end{array} as a labeled row-name column immediately after a bracketed matrix, itself nested inside an outer \begin{aligned} row): the inner block's own colspec ('cc') and its own \end{array}/\begin{array} tokens leaked onto the page as literal visible text ('...cc रामकिशन', 'गुरुचरण सिंह array...') because the outer split severed the nested block's opening tag from its own closing tag at the wrong point.
